newsitem.title: UK: Major, Blair remember the horror of Dunblane.
newsitem.headline: Major, Blair remember the horror of Dunblane.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major and opposition Labour leader Tony Blair set aside pre-election battles on Thursday and united in solemn memory of the 16 children murdered in Dunblane a year ago.
Both men paid tribute to the children and their teacher gunned down in a school gymnasium in the Scottish town by crazed loner Thomas Hamilton.
"I am sure the thoughts not only of this House of Commons, but of the entire nation are with them (the people of Dunblane) today," Major told parliament.
He recalled he had travelled with Blair to Dunblane to offer sympathy and comfort in the aftermath of the tragedy which appalled Britain.
"I do not believe that either of us will ever forget the scenes that we saw there, and neither will anyone else who visited it," said Major.
Earlier Blair told a silent parliament that those who died would never be forgotten by the British people.
"One year ago this house stood united in shock at the senseless and appalling tragedy at Dunblane," he said.
"Today, whatever our differences are in any other matter, we are united again, this time in sorrow and in commemoration of those that died."
The ruling Conservatives and opposition parties have already started gearing up for a general election which Major must call by May.
